title: Target anatomy
view: Transverse section of the right mid-forearm, palm up, under a linear probe on the volar-ulnar side, as on ultrasound: radial (FDS) on the image left, ulnar (FCU, ulna) on the right, volar skin at the top - the same way round as the median section. Composition after NYSORA's plate (concept only).
teachingPoint: Deep to FCU the ulnar nerve lies just medial to the ulnar artery in the same fascial plane; the needle comes in from the medial side and the spread surrounds the nerve and reaches the nerve/artery border.
claims: Probe transverse on the volar forearm over the ulnar artery (record).
Nerve directly medial to the artery, oval, deep to FCU, in the same fascial plane as the artery (record).
FDS radial, FCU ulnar and superficial with its tendon just over the artery, FDP deep, ulna under FDP on the ulnar side (standard anatomy; NYSORA note on the FCU tendon).
Needle in-plane from the medial (ulnar) side, tip at the medial surface of the nerve (record).
Teal: spread around the nerve and up to the nerve/artery border (record).
Labels: Ulnar nerve, Ulnar artery, Flexor carpi ulnaris, FDS, FDP, Ulna.

geometry.why: nerve medial (ulnar, image right) to the artery
nerve in the fascial plane, not in fat
needle in-plane from the medial side
tip beside, not into, the nerve
spread reaches the nerve/artery border from the nerve side
